title: The Cook–Levin Theorem and the Birth of NP-Completeness (1971)
explainer: In 1971 Stephen Cook published "The Complexity of Theorem Proving Procedures," proving that Boolean satisfiability (SAT) is NP-complete; the Soviet mathematician Leonid Levin independently proved an equivalent result around the same period, working in isolation from Western research. Richard Karp's follow-up paper then showed that 21 other well-known problems reduce to SAT, which is why a single reduction can show a brand-new problem is "as hard as" a thousand others instead of needing to be analyzed from scratch.
